No, lifetime rose about 25%, not 100%. With constant monthly churn, expected lifetime is 1/churn: 1/0.05 = 20 months, 1/0.04 = 25 months. Doubling would need churn to fall to 2.5%.

It's still a real improvement, since LTV rises by the same 25% at constant margin. But the 1/churn formula assumes a constant rate, and churn is usually front-loaded, so check cohort retention curves before trusting the 25%. Also confirm the drop isn't one noisy month, especially with a small customer base.
